source.title: On the Heavy-Tailed Theory of Stochastic Gradient Descent for Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Umut Simsekli; M. Gürbüzbalaban; T. Nguyen; G. Richard; Levent Sagun

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study examines test error against gradient-noise scale and tail index, and reports that the test-error trend does not support attributing performance improvement to lower tail index. It does not test the listed versions’ specific interventions or measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper measures gradient-noise tail behavior across architectures, sizes, datasets, losses, batch sizes, and iterations. Most of those measurements concern the noise distribution rather than the claim versions’ named outcomes. The generalization section reports test-error trends and correlations against noise scale and tail index; results are figure-only.
record.test_reason: The study tests heavy-tailed gradient-noise models and their association with test error, rather than any listed version. It does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness (V7). Its batch-size experiments use fixed iteration limits or stop at perfect training accuracy, without establishing the fixed epoch comparison required by V5. Varying η/b also combines learning-rate and batch-size changes.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report strongly non-Gaussian, heavy-tailed gradient noise, develop a Lévy-driven account of SGD dynamics and local convergence, and find loss-dependent tail-index/test-error associations that prevent attributing improved performance uniformly to lower tail index.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates heavy-tailed gradient noise and its relation to SGD dynamics and generalization; it does not implement the claim versions’ listed experiments. In the minibatch-size experiment, the paper states that train and test accuracies were the same across minibatch sizes, without giving numeric values or an epoch-budget comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The test-error and tail-index trends with η/b depend on the choice of loss function; the paper reports positive and negative correlations across the two loss choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Test error improves with increasing η/b over the studied range, but its correlation with gradient-noise tail index has opposite directions for the two losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The association between gradient-noise tail index and held-out performance depends on the loss function in this MNIST setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6.3 reports the same training and test accuracies across minibatch sizes, without a fixed epoch comparison or numerical accuracy values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different minibatch sizes can yield equal accuracies under this study's training protocol.

record.problems: The generalization results are presented in figures without exact values, uncertainty estimates, or correlation coefficients. Test-error values are averaged over candidates grouped by η/b. The authors say to focus on trends rather than particular test-error values.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the many architecture, width, depth, dataset, batch-size, layer, and iteration tail-index estimates: those outcomes measure gradient-noise properties rather than a version’s named generalization measure. Section 6.3 states train and test accuracies were the same across minibatch sizes, but gives no separate numeric outcomes or fixed-epoch comparison; this is noted in recipe_differences.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Continued test-error improvement beyond the width needed for zero training error in the specified fully connected networks. The CNN width plots do not establish this comparison.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected test performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance and tuning-dependent differences.
Large-batch held-out penalties under fixed epoch budgets and their recovery through recipe changes.
Effects of adding or removing dropout on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance versus generalization gap, including comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: T5 is unwarranted: qualifying a proposed tail-index explanation does not qualify any listed claim version. The batch-size accuracy result is already declared in rows_left_out, so it is not a missing result.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test-error scaling beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local connectivity.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
